intro.headline: Electrical Engineer (US EI/EiT) | Software Engineer | HU Walton Alumnus

about.introduction: This space showcases systems and projects I've built at the intersection of hardware, software, and infrastructure. I graduated Cum Laude as a Walton Scholar from Harding University (AR, US) with an ABET-accredited B.S. in Electrical Engineering, a minor in Mathematics, and passed the NCEES FE Exam prior to graduation, which enabled me to receive a US EI/EiT license. My work spans embedded systems, power and PCB design, automation, and software development, with a strong emphasis on documentation, long-term maintainability, and practical solutions designed to perform reliably beyond the lab environment.

iassc.name: Lean Six Sigma Green Belt
iassc.summary: Senior-level Lean Six Sigma Green Belt-aligned coursework completed at Harding University, emphasizing process improvement, statistical analysis, and data-driven decision making.
iassc.details: Completed ENGR-4550 (Lean Six Sigma) during Spring 2025 as a senior-level engineering elective at Harding University, earning an A. The course was taught following American Society for Quality (ASQ) Lean Six Sigma Green Belt standards and covered DMAIC, statistical process control, root cause analysis, process optimization, and waste reduction across engineering and operational contexts. IASSC Lean Six Sigma Green Belt certification is planned for 2026.

arpels.name: Engineer Intern (EI/EiT)
arpels.summary: Engineer in Training (EI/EIT) status obtained through successful completion of the NCEES Fundamentals of Engineering (FE) exam.
arpels.details: The Engineer in Training (EI/EIT) credential signifies completion of an ABET-accredited engineering degree and passing the NCEES FE examination. It represents the first formal step toward Professional Engineer (PE) licensure and demonstrates verified competency in core engineering fundamentals, ethics, and professional responsibility.

hu.name: B.S. Electrical Engineering
hu.summary: Bachelor of Science in Electrical Engineering (Cum Laude), ABET-accredited program.
hu.details: Completed a Bachelor of Science in Electrical Engineering from Harding University, an ABET-accredited institution, graduating Cum Laude with a 3.7/4.0 GPA. Academic focus included power systems, electronics, microprocessors, control systems, and applied mathematics, alongside extensive project-based engineering design work.

cs50.name: CS50x
cs50.summary: Rigorous introduction to computer science and software engineering fundamentals from Harvard University, completed with Honors.
cs50.details: CS50 is Harvard University's flagship introduction to computer science, completed with Honors. The course covers algorithms, data structures, memory management, abstraction, and core software engineering principles, with an emphasis on problem-solving and low-level understanding of computation. Coursework spans C, Python, SQL, JavaScript, HTML, and CSS.

coursera.name: Solving Problems with Software (Java)
coursera.summary: Applied Java programming and algorithmic problem-solving through Duke University’s computer science curriculum, completed with Honors.
coursera.details: Completed with Honors, this Duke University course focuses on solving real-world problems using Java, emphasizing algorithmic thinking, data processing, debugging, and program design. The course centers on translating problem statements into correct, efficient, and maintainable software solutions.

ncees.issuer: National Council of Examiners for Engineering and Surveying (US NCEES)

awards.title: Honor Graduate
awards.summary: Passed the NCEES Fundamentals of Engineering Exam while still an undergraduate, qualifying for official NCEES Honor Graduate recognition — an early milestone toward professional engineering licensure.
awards.details: Current engineering and surveying students who pass the FE or FS exam prior to graduating from a participating program are eligible to receive a free NCEES honor cord to wear at their graduation ceremony. To receive a cord, students must select the appropriate option during the exam registration process and receive notification of passing results on the exam at least 21 days before their graduation date.

awards.title: Walton Scholar
awards.summary: Awarded the Walton International Scholarship, a highly competitive, full-tuition merit scholarship for top international students, enabling a debt-free undergraduate education.
awards.details: Founded in 1985 by Sam and Helen Walton, the Walton International Scholarship Program (WISP) provides free college education for the brightest and most capable students from Central America, Belize, and Mexico.

awards.title: Cum Laude Graduate
awards.summary: Graduated with Cum Laude honors in Electrical Engineering, recognizing sustained academic excellence across a rigorous ABET-accredited curriculum.
awards.details: Graduated with Cum Laude honors in the Bachelor of Science in Electrical Engineering program, awarded to students who demonstrate consistent high academic performance across their undergraduate coursework. This distinction reflects a cumulative GPA of 3.7 on a 4.0 scale, achieved while completing an ABET-accredited engineering curriculum emphasizing advanced mathematics, circuit analysis, power systems, electronics, control systems, and embedded computing.

awards.title: Distinguished Scholar
awards.summary: Selected as a Distinguished Scholar for exceptional academic performance and interdisciplinary excellence within Harding University's competitive American Studies Institute program.
awards.details: Harding University students of all majors are eligible to apply to the American Studies Institute Distinguished Scholars program. The prerequisites for automatic invitation include a 3.8-grade point average or above and standing as a junior, senior, or freshman member of Harding University's Honors Scholar Program. Each fall there is an open application process for those with an automatic invitation and those who have a 3.6-grade point average.

awards.title: Honor Student
awards.summary: Admitted to and maintained standing in the Honors College, a selective program representing approximately 10% of the undergraduate population and emphasizing academic rigor, leadership, and service.
awards.details: The Honors College annually admits around 100 students, bringing its total enrollment to approximately 400, representing about 10% of Harding's undergraduate student body, in line with national norms for honors education. Honors students must maintain a 3.25 GPA, are encouraged to pursue Honors College recognition at graduation, and are expected to engage in leadership and service at the University and/or in the community.

awards.title: Dean's List
awards.summary: Recognized on the Dean's List on multiple semesters for achieving a semester GPA of 3.65 or higher while carrying a full academic course load.
awards.details: The dean's list is published each semester by Dr. Marty Spears, University provost, honoring those who have achieved high scholarship. To be eligible, a student must be carrying 12 or more hours with a 3.65 or higher grade-point average and no incompletes.
